title: A create whose podman run fails leaves its two volumes, and ls then lists a sandbox nobody removed
foundBy: session agent, 2026-11-16, while a gVisor experiment's `create --privileged` failed at `podman run`
details:
`Podman.Create` (internal/engine/podman.go) returns as soon as `podman run` fails. The deferred reap that removes a partial sandbox is armed only after the run succeeds. Podman has already created the named volumes the run mounts by then, `cs-sandbox-home-<name>.<group>` and `cs-sandbox-containers-<name>.<group>`, so both stay. `ls` reads a home volume with no instance as data `rm` kept, and lists the name as `removed`.

Seen on 2026-11-16 in an experiment group: `create gp1 --group gvexp2 --privileged` under gVisor failed at `podman run`, and `group rm gvexp2 -f` then left both volumes. To reproduce, make `podman run` fail after it has parsed its volumes, for example with a runtime that refuses the container. A create that never ran should leave nothing behind, so the reap belongs before the run, scoped to volumes this create made (`reusingData` already tells the two apart).
